2.1 Governing Policy. The procedures in this manual are adopted pursuant to Policy 504-2021-01, as amended, which is the District’s foundational policy on accessibility services. Policy 504-2021-01 establishes the District’s commitment to non-discrimination and sets forth the administrative framework for implementing the requirements of Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, Title II of the Americans with Disabilities Act, and applicable state law.

2.2 Supersession. Policy 504-2021-01 supersedes all prior District policies and procedures regarding accessibility services to the extent they are inconsistent. Any conflicting provisions in school-level handbooks, site plans, or other local documents are subordinate to this manual and to Policy 504-2021-01.

2.3 Interpretation. This manual is intended to be interpreted consistently with Policy 504-2021-01. In the event of a conflict between this manual and the policy, the policy shall control. Questions regarding interpretation shall be directed to the Accessibility Coordinator.

SECTION 3: GENERAL ACCESSIBILITY PRINCIPLES

3.1 Non-Discrimination. The District shall not, on the basis of disability, exclude any qualified individual with a disability from participation in, or deny the benefits of, any District service, program, or activity, or subject such individual to discrimination.

3.2 Equal Opportunity. The District shall provide individuals with disabilities an equal opportunity to participate in and benefit from District programs, services, and activities, including extracurricular activities, athletics, field trips, and community events held on District property.

3.3 Integration. The District shall provide services, programs, and activities in the most integrated setting appropriate to the needs of the individual, unless a separate or different measure is necessary to ensure equal opportunity.

3.4 Effective Communication. The District shall take appropriate steps to ensure that communication with individuals with disabilities is as effective as communication with others. This includes furnishing appropriate auxiliary aids and services where necessary to afford an individual with a disability an equal opportunity to participate in and enjoy the benefits of a District service, program, or activity.

Sunrise Unified School District has_policy_number 504-2021-01. Record status: superseded.

3.5 Reasonable Modifications. The District shall make reasonable modifications to policies, practices, and procedures when necessary to avoid discrimination on the basis of disability, unless the District can demonstrate that making the modification would fundamentally alter the nature of the service, program, or activity.

3.6 Program Accessibility. The District shall operate each service, program, or activity so that, when viewed in its entirety, it is readily accessible to and usable by individuals with disabilities. This requirement does not necessarily require the District to make each of its existing facilities accessible, provided that the program as a whole is accessible.

3.7 Maintenance of Accessible Features. The District shall maintain in operable working condition those features of facilities and equipment that are required to be accessible. This includes, but is not limited to, accessible routes, ramps, elevators, restrooms, parking spaces, signage, and assistive listening systems. Isolated or temporary interruptions in service due to maintenance or repair shall be remedied promptly.

3.8 Designation of Responsibility. The Superintendent has designated the Accessibility Coordinator to carry out the responsibilities set forth in this manual. The Accessibility Coordinator shall report directly to the Superintendent and shall have the authority to coordinate all accessibility efforts across the District.

SECTION 4: APPLICABILITY AND EXCEPTIONS

4.1 Who is Covered. The protections and accommodations described in this manual apply to:

(a) Students with disabilities, including those who have not been identified as eligible for special education services under the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA) but who have a disability as defined in Section 1.3(c);
(a) instructional programs, including general education, special education, career and technical education, and adult education;
(b) extracurricular and athletic programs;
(c) before- and after-school care and enrichment programs;
(d) parent and community engagement activities;
(e) transportation services;
(f) food services;
(g) counseling and health services;
(h) library and media services; and
(i) any other District-sponsored or District-operated activity, whether conducted on school grounds, at a District facility, or at another location.

4.3 Contracted Services. Where the District contracts with a third party to provide a service, program, or activity, the contract shall include provisions requiring the third party to comply with the accessibility requirements set forth in this manual and applicable federal and state law. The Accessibility Coordinator shall review contract language upon request and may recommend revisions to ensure compliance.

4.4 Exceptions. The District is not required to take any action that it can demonstrate would result in a fundamental alteration in the nature of a service, program, or activity, or in undue financial and administrative burdens. In such cases, the District shall nevertheless take any other action that would not result in such an alteration or such burdens but would nevertheless ensure to the maximum extent possible that individuals with disabilities receive the benefits or services provided by the District.

4.5 Documentation of Exception Determinations. Any determination that a proposed modification or accommodation would cause a fundamental alteration or undue burden shall be made in writing by the Superintendent or designee, after consideration of all resources available for use in the funding and operation of the service, program, or activity. The written determination shall include the reasons for reaching the conclusion that a fundamental alteration or undue burden would result, and shall be retained in the office of the Accessibility Coordinator.

SECTION 5: IMPLEMENTATION TIMELINE

All provisions of this manual, including the requirements for reasonable modifications, program accessibility, and the designation of the Accessibility Coordinator, take effect on that date.

5.2 Transition Plan. Within ninety (90) days of the effective date, the Accessibility Coordinator shall prepare and submit to the Superintendent a transition plan identifying any structural, programmatic, or communication barriers to accessibility that remain in District facilities, programs, or services. The transition plan shall include:

(a) a schedule for achieving program accessibility, including any necessary structural changes;
(b) a description of the methods to be used to make the changes; and
(c) a timeline for completing each identified action.

5.3 Interim Procedures. From the date this manual is adopted until the effective date, the District shall continue to implement its prior accessibility procedures and shall process requests for accommodations and modifications on an interim basis. The Accessibility Coordinator shall ensure that all staff responsible for receiving such requests are informed of the interim procedures and of the upcoming effective date.

5.4 Staff Training. The Accessibility Coordinator, in coordination with the Human Resources Department, shall develop and deliver training on the requirements of this manual. Training shall be provided to the following groups no later than sixty (60) days after the effective date:

(a) all school principals and assistant principals;
(b) all staff with responsibility for receiving or responding to accommodation requests;
(c) all staff involved in the planning or delivery of District programs, services, or activities, including but not limited to athletic directors, activities directors, transportation supervisors, food services managers, and custodial supervisors; and
(d) all staff responsible for facilities maintenance and construction.

### 6.4 Filing a Grievance

A grievance must be filed in writing and must include:

(a) the name, address, and contact information of the complainant;
(b) a description of the alleged discriminatory act or practice, including the date(s) and location(s) of the act or practice;
(c) the name(s) of the individual(s) or office(s) alleged to have committed the discriminatory act or practice, if known;
(d) the specific disability-related basis of the complaint, if known;
(e) the remedy or corrective action requested; and
(f) the signature of the complainant and the date of filing.

Grievances may be submitted by mail, email, or in person to the Grievance Coordinator. A grievance may be filed on behalf of a student or other person by a parent, guardian, or authorized representative. The Grievance Coordinator shall assist any complainant who requests assistance in preparing a written grievance, including providing interpretation or translation services as needed.

A grievance must be filed within one hundred eighty (180) calendar days of the alleged discriminatory act or practice, or from the date the complainant knew or reasonably should have known of the act or practice. The Grievance Coordinator may extend this deadline for good cause shown.

### 6.5 Investigation and Resolution

Upon receipt of a grievance, the Grievance Coordinator shall:

(a) acknowledge receipt of the grievance in writing within five (5) business days;
(b) assign an investigator who has no conflict of interest with respect to the matter;
(c) conduct a thorough and impartial investigation, which may include interviews with the complainant, the respondent, and any witnesses, and review of relevant documents and records;
(d) provide the complainant and the respondent with an opportunity to present evidence and to respond to the allegations;
(e) issue a written decision to the complainant and the respondent within forty-five (45) calendar days of receipt of the grievance, unless the parties agree to an extension or the Grievance Coordinator determines that additional time is necessary and notifies the parties in writing.

The written decision shall include:

(i) a summary of the allegations;
(ii) a summary of the investigation conducted;
(iii) findings of fact;
(iv) a determination as to whether discrimination on the basis of disability occurred; and
(v) if discrimination is found, a description of the corrective action to be taken, including any remedies for the complainant and any steps to prevent recurrence.

### 6.6 Appeal

Either party may appeal the Grievance Coordinator's decision by filing a written notice of appeal with the Superintendent within fifteen (15) business days of receipt of the decision. The Superintendent, or a designee who did not participate in the initial investigation, shall review the record and may conduct additional investigation as deemed necessary. The Superintendent shall issue a written decision on the appeal within thirty (30) calendar days of receipt of the notice of appeal. The decision of the Superintendent shall be final.

### 6.7 Confidentiality

All grievances, investigations, and related records shall be kept confidential to the extent permitted by law. Information may be disclosed to individuals with a legitimate need to know in order to investigate and resolve the grievance, or as required by law or court order.

### 6.8 Retaliation Prohibited

The District prohibits retaliation against any individual who, in good faith, files a grievance, participates in an investigation, or otherwise exercises rights under this procedure. Any act of retaliation shall be subject to disciplinary action, up to and including dismissal or expulsion, as appropriate.

### 6.9 Alternative Remedies
### 6.9 Alternative Remedies

Nothing in this procedure shall prevent the complainant from pursuing other available remedies, including but not limited to filing a complaint with the U.S. Department of Education, Office for Civil Rights, or with any other federal, state, or local agency with jurisdiction. The District encourages the prompt resolution of concerns at the lowest possible level and will make reasonable efforts to facilitate informal resolution where appropriate, provided that such efforts do not delay the formal grievance process beyond the timelines established in this procedure.

### 6.10 Record Keeping

The Grievance Coordinator shall maintain a central log of all grievances filed under this procedure, including the date of filing, the nature of the allegation, the status of the investigation, the final disposition, and any corrective action taken. Records shall be retained for a minimum of seven (7) years in accordance with the District's records retention schedule. Aggregate data regarding grievances shall be reviewed annually by the Superintendent or designee to identify patterns that may indicate systemic barriers to accessibility.

## SECTION 7: ACCOMMODATION REQUEST PROCEDURES

### 7.1 Overview

The District provides reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities to ensure equal access to District programs, services, and activities. Accommodations may include modifications to policies, practices, or procedures; provision of auxiliary aids and services; and physical or structural changes to facilities. This section describes the process for requesting and receiving accommodations for students, parents/guardians, visitors, and members of the public.

### 7.2 Who May Request an Accommodation

Any individual with a disability, or an individual acting on behalf of a person with a disability, may request an accommodation. For students, the request may be made by a parent, guardian, or other individual with legal authority to act on the student's behalf. For employees, requests are processed through the Human Resources Department in accordance with applicable law and District policy. This section applies to non-employment accommodations.

### 7.3 How to Submit a Request

Requests for accommodation may be submitted verbally or in writing. Verbal requests shall be documented by the District staff member receiving the request and forwarded to the appropriate Accommodations Coordinator. Requests may be submitted to any of the following:

- The school principal or designee;
- The student's teacher or counselor;
- The Section 504 Coordinator;
- The Accessibility Services Office; or
- Any other District employee who regularly interacts with the public.

The individual making the request is not required to use specific language, reference any law, or submit a formal form to initiate the process. However, the District may ask for information necessary to evaluate the request, including documentation of the disability and the specific barrier or limitation experienced.

### 7.4 Role of the Accommodations Coordinator

Each school and department shall designate an Accommodations Coordinator, who may be the same individual as the Section 504 Coordinator or another trained staff member. The Accommodations Coordinator is responsible for:

- Receiving and documenting accommodation requests;
- Conducting an individualized assessment of each request;
- Engaging in an interactive process with the requester;
- Identifying and implementing appropriate accommodations;
- Maintaining records of requests and outcomes; and
- Coordinating with other District departments as needed.

### 7.5 The Interactive Process

Upon receipt of a request, the Accommodations Coordinator shall engage in a timely, good-faith interactive process with the requester to determine what accommodations, if any, are necessary and appropriate. The process shall include:

(i) An assessment of the nature of the disability and the barriers experienced;
(ii) A review of the specific programs, services, or activities at issue;
(iii) Consultation with the requester regarding potential accommodations; and
(iv) Consideration of alternative accommodations if the requested accommodation would pose an undue hardship or a fundamental alteration.

### 7.6 Documentation and Confidentiality

All documentation related to an accommodation request, including medical records, assessment notes, and correspondence, shall be maintained in a confidential file separate from the student's general education record. Access to these files shall be limited to:

- The Accommodations Coordinator;
- The Section 504 Coordinator;
- The building principal or designee;
- The Superintendent or designee; and
- Other District staff with a legitimate educational interest, as determined by the Accommodations Coordinator.

Records shall be retained for a period of seven (7) years following the conclusion of the accommodation, or until the student reaches the age of twenty-five (25), whichever is later. Requests for access to accommodation records by the student, parent, or guardian shall be processed in accordance with the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA) and District Policy 724.

The District shall not disclose the existence of an accommodation request or the nature of an accommodation to any third party without the written consent of the student (if eighteen or older) or the parent/guardian, except as required by law or as necessary to implement the accommodation. This prohibition does not extend to disclosures made to District employees who are directly involved in the implementation or evaluation of the accommodation.

### 7.7 Emergency and Temporary Accommodations

In cases where a student or member of the public experiences a sudden injury, medical event, or other temporary condition that substantially limits one or more major life activities, the District shall provide interim accommodations to ensure access while a formal evaluation is pending. Interim accommodations may include, but are not limited to:

- Temporary seating changes;
- Extended time for assignments or tests;
- Provision of assistive technology on a short-term basis;
- Relocation of classes or events to accessible areas; and
- Permission for service animals on a temporary basis.

The Accommodations Coordinator shall review the interim accommodation within fifteen (15) school days of its implementation to determine whether a formal accommodation plan is necessary. Interim accommodations shall not be used to delay an otherwise timely evaluation.

### 7.8 Denial, Appeal, and Grievance

If a request for accommodation is denied, in whole or in part, the Accommodations Coordinator shall provide the requester with a written notice of denial that includes:

- The specific reason(s) for the denial;
- A description of any alternative accommodations considered;
- An explanation of the interactive process conducted; and
- Information on how to appeal the decision.

A denial may be appealed by submitting a written notice to the Section 504 Coordinator within fifteen (15) school days of receipt of the denial notice. The Section 504 Coordinator, or a designee who was not involved in the original decision, shall review the denial and issue a written decision within twenty (20) school days of receipt of the appeal.

Nothing in this section shall be construed to limit the right of a student, parent, or guardian to file a complaint with the Office for Civil Rights (OCR) of the U.S. Department of Education, or to pursue any other remedy available under federal, state, or local law.

## SECTION 8: TRAINING AND ROLES

### 8.1 General Training Requirements

The District shall provide ongoing training on accessibility obligations to all employees, contractors, and volunteers who interact with the public or who are involved in the delivery of District programs, services, or activities. The purpose of this training is to ensure that all personnel understand:

- The legal obligations of the District under the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, and applicable state law;
- The procedures for receiving and responding to accommodation requests;
- The proper use of assistive technology and accessible materials;
- The principles of effective communication, including the use of interpreters and auxiliary aids; and
- The District's policies regarding confidentiality and non-discrimination.
# SECTION 8: TRAINING AND ROLES (continued)

### 8.2 Training Content and Frequency

All training provided under Section 8.1 shall be delivered prior to an employee assuming duties that involve interaction with the public or the delivery of District programs, services, or activities, and at least annually thereafter. The Accommodations Coordinator, in consultation with the Human Resources Department, shall maintain a schedule of required training and shall track completion for all personnel.

The following table identifies the minimum training requirements by role:

| Role | Initial Training | Annual Refresher | Additional Requirements |
|------|------------------|------------------|-------------------------|
| Teachers and instructional aides | Yes | Yes | Training on accessible instructional materials and classroom accommodations |
| School administrators | Yes | Yes | Training on Section 504 procedures, IEP coordination, and grievance handling |
| Front office and clerical staff | Yes | Yes | Training on receiving accommodation requests and effective communication |
| Transportation staff | Yes | Yes | Training on wheelchair securement and assistance for students with disabilities |
| Custodial and facilities staff | Yes | Yes | Training on accessible route maintenance and emergency evacuation procedures |
| Food service staff | Yes | Yes | Training on dietary accommodations and service to students with disabilities |
| Substitute personnel | Yes | No | Brief orientation on accessibility procedures before first assignment |
| Contractors and volunteers | Yes | No | Training appropriate to the scope of their work with the District |

All training sessions shall include an opportunity for questions and shall provide written or electronic materials that participants may keep for reference. The District shall maintain records of attendance, training dates, and materials used for a period of at least five (5) years.

### 8.3 Specialized Training

In addition to the general training requirements, the following personnel shall receive specialized training:

- **Accommodations Coordinator and Section 504 Coordinator**: Training on federal and state disability laws, the interactive process, reasonable accommodation determinations, and dispute resolution, to be completed within six (6) months of assuming the role and at least biennially thereafter.
- **School psychologists and evaluation staff**: Training on appropriate assessment instruments, cultural and linguistic considerations, and documentation standards for disability determinations.
- **Technology staff**: Training on web accessibility standards (including WCAG 2.1 Level AA), accessible document creation, and the procurement of accessible technology.
- **Interpreters and captioners**: Training on the District's policies regarding confidentiality, professional conduct, and emergency procedures.

The District may provide specialized training through external providers, online courses, or in-house sessions. The Accommodations Coordinator shall approve all specialized training content and shall maintain a list of approved providers.

### 8.4 New Employee Orientation

All new employees shall receive an overview of the District's accessibility policies as part of new employee orientation. This overview shall include:

- A summary of the District's non-discrimination policies;
- An explanation of how to recognize and respond to accommodation requests;
- Contact information for the Accommodations Coordinator and Section 504 Coordinator;
- An introduction to assistive technology available in the District; and
- Instructions for accessing the full text of this Manual.

The Human Resources Department shall ensure that new employee orientation includes the accessibility overview and shall document attendance.

### 8.5 Training Evaluation

The District shall evaluate the effectiveness of its training program on an annual basis. Methods of evaluation may include pre- and post-training assessments, surveys of participants, and review of accommodation request outcomes. The results of these evaluations shall be summarized in a written report to the Superintendent and shall inform revisions to the training program.

2.1 Governing Policy. The procedures in this manual are adopted pursuant to Policy 504-2021-01, as amended, which is the District’s foundational policy on accessibility services. Policy 504-2021-01 establishes the District’s commitment to non-discrimination and sets forth the administrative framework for implementing the requirements of Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, Title II of the Americans with Disabilities Act, and applicable state law.

2.2 Supersession. Policy 504-2021-01 supersedes all prior District policies and procedures regarding accessibility services to the extent they are inconsistent. Any conflicting provisions in school-level handbooks, site plans, or other local documents are subordinate to this manual and to Policy 504-2021-01.

2.3 Interpretation. This manual is intended to be interpreted consistently with Policy 504-2021-01. In the event of a conflict between this manual and the policy, the policy shall control. Questions regarding interpretation shall be directed to the Accessibility Coordinator.

SECTION 3: GENERAL ACCESSIBILITY PRINCIPLES

3.1 Non-Discrimination. The District shall not, on the basis of disability, exclude any qualified individual with a disability from participation in, or deny the benefits of, any District service, program, or activity, or subject such individual to discrimination.

3.2 Equal Opportunity. The District shall provide individuals with disabilities an equal opportunity to participate in and benefit from District programs, services, and activities, including extracurricular activities, athletics, field trips, and community events held on District property.

3.3 Integration. The District shall provide services, programs, and activities in the most integrated setting appropriate to the needs of the individual, unless a separate or different measure is necessary to ensure equal opportunity.

3.4 Effective Communication. The District shall take appropriate steps to ensure that communication with individuals with disabilities is as effective as communication with others. This includes furnishing appropriate auxiliary aids and services where necessary to afford an individual with a disability an equal opportunity to participate in and enjoy the benefits of a District service, program, or activity.

Sunrise Unified School District has_policy_number 504-2021-01. Record status: superseded.

3.5 Reasonable Modifications. The District shall make reasonable modifications to policies, practices, and procedures when necessary to avoid discrimination on the basis of disability, unless the District can demonstrate that making the modification would fundamentally alter the nature of the service, program, or activity.

3.6 Program Accessibility. The District shall operate each service, program, or activity so that, when viewed in its entirety, it is readily accessible to and usable by individuals with disabilities. This requirement does not necessarily require the District to make each of its existing facilities accessible, provided that the program as a whole is accessible.

3.7 Maintenance of Accessible Features. The District shall maintain in operable working condition those features of facilities and equipment that are required to be accessible. This includes, but is not limited to, accessible routes, ramps, elevators, restrooms, parking spaces, signage, and assistive listening systems. Isolated or temporary interruptions in service due to maintenance or repair shall be remedied promptly.

3.8 Designation of Responsibility. The Superintendent has designated the Accessibility Coordinator to carry out the responsibilities set forth in this manual. The Accessibility Coordinator shall report directly to the Superintendent and shall have the authority to coordinate all accessibility efforts across the District.

### 6.4 Filing a Grievance

A grievance must be filed in writing and must include:

(a) the name, address, and contact information of the complainant;
(b) a description of the alleged discriminatory act or practice, including the date(s) and location(s) of the act or practice;
(c) the name(s) of the individual(s) or office(s) alleged to have committed the discriminatory act or practice, if known;
(d) the specific disability-related basis of the complaint, if known;
(e) the remedy or corrective action requested; and
(f) the signature of the complainant and the date of filing.

Grievances may be submitted by mail, email, or in person to the Grievance Coordinator. A grievance may be filed on behalf of a student or other person by a parent, guardian, or authorized representative. The Grievance Coordinator shall assist any complainant who requests assistance in preparing a written grievance, including providing interpretation or translation services as needed.

A grievance must be filed within one hundred eighty (180) calendar days of the alleged discriminatory act or practice, or from the date the complainant knew or reasonably should have known of the act or practice. The Grievance Coordinator may extend this deadline for good cause shown.

### 6.5 Investigation and Resolution

Upon receipt of a grievance, the Grievance Coordinator shall:

(a) acknowledge receipt of the grievance in writing within five (5) business days;
(b) assign an investigator who has no conflict of interest with respect to the matter;
(c) conduct a thorough and impartial investigation, which may include interviews with the complainant, the respondent, and any witnesses, and review of relevant documents and records;
(d) provide the complainant and the respondent with an opportunity to present evidence and to respond to the allegations;
(e) issue a written decision to the complainant and the respondent within forty-five (45) calendar days of receipt of the grievance, unless the parties agree to an extension or the Grievance Coordinator determines that additional time is necessary and notifies the parties in writing.

The written decision shall include:

(i) a summary of the allegations;
(ii) a summary of the investigation conducted;
(iii) findings of fact;
(iv) a determination as to whether discrimination on the basis of disability occurred; and
(v) if discrimination is found, a description of the corrective action to be taken, including any remedies for the complainant and any steps to prevent recurrence.

### 6.6 Appeal

Either party may appeal the Grievance Coordinator's decision by filing a written notice of appeal with the Superintendent within fifteen (15) business days of receipt of the decision. The Superintendent, or a designee who did not participate in the initial investigation, shall review the record and may conduct additional investigation as deemed necessary. The Superintendent shall issue a written decision on the appeal within thirty (30) calendar days of receipt of the notice of appeal. The decision of the Superintendent shall be final.

### 6.7 Confidentiality

All grievances, investigations, and related records shall be kept confidential to the extent permitted by law. Information may be disclosed to individuals with a legitimate need to know in order to investigate and resolve the grievance, or as required by law or court order.

### 6.8 Retaliation Prohibited

The District prohibits retaliation against any individual who, in good faith, files a grievance, participates in an investigation, or otherwise exercises rights under this procedure. Any act of retaliation shall be subject to disciplinary action, up to and including dismissal or expulsion, as appropriate.

### 6.9 Alternative Remedies

Nothing in this procedure shall prevent the complainant from pursuing other available remedies, including but not limited to filing a complaint with the U.S. Department of Education, Office for Civil Rights, or with any other federal, state, or local agency with jurisdiction. The District encourages the prompt resolution of concerns at the lowest possible level and will make reasonable efforts to facilitate informal resolution where appropriate, provided that such efforts do not delay the formal grievance process beyond the timelines established in this procedure.

### 6.10 Record Keeping

The Grievance Coordinator shall maintain a central log of all grievances filed under this procedure, including the date of filing, the nature of the allegation, the status of the investigation, the final disposition, and any corrective action taken. Records shall be retained for a minimum of seven (7) years in accordance with the District's records retention schedule. Aggregate data regarding grievances shall be reviewed annually by the Superintendent or designee to identify patterns that may indicate systemic barriers to accessibility.

---

## SECTION 7: ACCOMMODATION REQUEST PROCEDURES

### 7.1 Overview

The District provides reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities to ensure equal access to District programs, services, and activities. Accommodations may include modifications to policies, practices, or procedures; provision of auxiliary aids and services; and physical or structural changes to facilities. This section describes the process for requesting and receiving accommodations for students, parents/guardians, visitors, and members of the public.

### 7.2 Who May Request an Accommodation

Any individual with a disability, or an individual acting on behalf of a person with a disability, may request an accommodation. For students, the request may be made by a parent, guardian, or other individual with legal authority to act on the student's behalf. For employees, requests are processed through the Human Resources Department in accordance with applicable law and District policy. This section applies to non-employment accommodations.

### 7.3 How to Submit a Request

Requests for accommodation may be submitted verbally or in writing. Verbal requests shall be documented by the District staff member receiving the request and forwarded to the appropriate Accommodations Coordinator. Requests may be submitted to any of the following:

- The school principal or designee;
- The student's teacher or counselor;
- The Section 504 Coordinator;
- The Accessibility Services Office; or
- Any other District employee who regularly interacts with the public.

The individual making the request is not required to use specific language, reference any law, or submit a formal form to initiate the process. However, the District may ask for information necessary to evaluate the request, including documentation of the disability and the specific barrier or limitation experienced.

### 7.4 Role of the Accommodations Coordinator

Each school and department shall designate an Accommodations Coordinator, who may be the same individual as the Section 504 Coordinator or another trained staff member. The Accommodations Coordinator is responsible for:

- Receiving and documenting accommodation requests;
- Conducting an individualized assessment of each request;
- Engaging in an interactive process with the requester;
- Identifying and implementing appropriate accommodations;
- Maintaining records of requests and outcomes; and
- Coordinating with other District departments as needed.

### 7.5 The Interactive Process

Upon receipt of a request, the Accommodations Coordinator shall engage in a timely, good-faith interactive process with the requester to determine what accommodations, if any, are necessary and appropriate. The process shall include:

(i) An assessment of the nature of the disability and the barriers experienced;
(ii) A review of the specific programs, services, or activities at issue;
(iii) Consultation with the requester regarding potential accommodations; and
(iv) Consideration of alternative accommodations if the requested accommodation would pose an undue hardship or a fundamental alteration.

### 7.6 Documentation and Confidentiality

All documentation related to an accommodation request, including medical records, assessment notes, and correspondence, shall be maintained in a confidential file separate from the student's general education record. Access to these files shall be limited to:

- The Accommodations Coordinator;
- The Section 504 Coordinator;
- The building principal or designee;
- The Superintendent or designee; and
- Other District staff with a legitimate educational interest, as determined by the Accommodations Coordinator.

Records shall be retained for a period of seven (7) years following the conclusion of the accommodation, or until the student reaches the age of twenty-five (25), whichever is later. Requests for access to accommodation records by the student, parent, or guardian shall be processed in accordance with the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA) and District Policy 724.

The District shall not disclose the existence of an accommodation request or the nature of an accommodation to any third party without the written consent of the student (if eighteen or older) or the parent/guardian, except as required by law or as necessary to implement the accommodation. This prohibition does not extend to disclosures made to District employees who are directly involved in the implementation or evaluation of the accommodation.

### 7.7 Emergency and Temporary Accommodations

In cases where a student or member of the public experiences a sudden injury, medical event, or other temporary condition that substantially limits one or more major life activities, the District shall provide interim accommodations to ensure access while a formal evaluation is pending. Interim accommodations may include, but are not limited to:

- Temporary seating changes;
- Extended time for assignments or tests;
- Provision of assistive technology on a short-term basis;
- Relocation of classes or events to accessible areas; and
- Permission for service animals on a temporary basis.

The Accommodations Coordinator shall review the interim accommodation within fifteen (15) school days of its implementation to determine whether a formal accommodation plan is necessary. Interim accommodations shall not be used to delay an otherwise timely evaluation.

### 7.8 Denial, Appeal, and Grievance

If a request for accommodation is denied, in whole or in part, the Accommodations Coordinator shall provide the requester with a written notice of denial that includes:

- The specific reason(s) for the denial;
- A description of any alternative accommodations considered;
- An explanation of the interactive process conducted; and
- Information on how to appeal the decision.

A denial may be appealed by submitting a written notice to the Section 504 Coordinator within fifteen (15) school days of receipt of the denial notice. The Section 504 Coordinator, or a designee who was not involved in the original decision, shall review the denial and issue a written decision within twenty (20) school days of receipt of the appeal.

Nothing in this section shall be construed to limit the right of a student, parent, or guardian to file a complaint with the Office for Civil Rights (OCR) of the U.S. Department of Education, or to pursue any other remedy available under federal, state, or local law.

---

## SECTION 8: TRAINING AND ROLES

### 8.1 General Training Requirements

The District shall provide ongoing training on accessibility obligations to all employees, contractors, and volunteers who interact with the public or who are involved in the delivery of District programs, services, or activities. The purpose of this training is to ensure that all personnel understand:

- The legal obligations of the District under the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, and applicable state law;
- The procedures for receiving and responding to accommodation requests;
- The proper use of assistive technology and accessible materials;
- The principles of effective communication, including the use of interpreters and auxiliary aids; and
- The District's policies regarding confidentiality and non-discrimination.

| Teachers and instructional aides | Yes | Yes | Training on accessible instructional materials and classroom accommodations |
| School administrators | Yes | Yes | Training on Section 504 procedures, IEP coordination, and grievance handling |
| Front office and clerical staff | Yes | Yes | Training on receiving accommodation requests and effective communication |
| Transportation staff | Yes | Yes | Training on wheelchair securement and assistance for students with disabilities |
| Custodial and facilities staff | Yes | Yes | Training on accessible route maintenance and emergency evacuation procedures |
| Food service staff | Yes | Yes | Training on dietary accommodations and service to students with disabilities |
| Substitute personnel | Yes | No | Brief orientation on accessibility procedures before first assignment |
| Contractors and volunteers | Yes | No | Training appropriate to the scope of their work with the District |

All training sessions shall include an opportunity for questions and shall provide written or electronic materials that participants may keep for reference. The District shall maintain records of attendance, training dates, and materials used for a period of at least five (5) years.

### 8.3 Specialized Training

In addition to the general training requirements, the following personnel shall receive specialized training:

- **Accommodations Coordinator and Section 504 Coordinator**: Training on federal and state disability laws, the interactive process, reasonable accommodation determinations, and dispute resolution, to be completed within six (6) months of assuming the role and at least biennially thereafter.
- **School psychologists and evaluation staff**: Training on appropriate assessment instruments, cultural and linguistic considerations, and documentation standards for disability determinations.
- **Technology staff**: Training on web accessibility standards (including WCAG 2.1 Level AA), accessible document creation, and the procurement of accessible technology.
- **Interpreters and captioners**: Training on the District's policies regarding confidentiality, professional conduct, and emergency procedures.

The District may provide specialized training through external providers, online courses, or in-house sessions. The Accommodations Coordinator shall approve all specialized training content and shall maintain a list of approved providers.

### 8.4 New Employee Orientation

All new employees shall receive an overview of the District's accessibility policies as part of new employee orientation. This overview shall include:

- A summary of the District's non-discrimination policies;
- An explanation of how to recognize and respond to accommodation requests;
- Contact information for the Accommodations Coordinator and Section 504 Coordinator;
- An introduction to assistive technology available in the District; and
- Instructions for accessing the full text of this Manual.

The Human Resources Department shall ensure that new employee orientation includes the accessibility overview and shall document attendance.

### 8.5 Training Evaluation

The District shall evaluate the effectiveness of its training program on an annual basis. Methods of evaluation may include pre- and post-training assessments, surveys of participants, and review of accommodation request outcomes. The results of these evaluations shall be summarized in a written report to the Superintendent and shall inform revisions to the training program.
